subproblem.title: Action and mass measure of the polygonal integer multiplicity triple (parent steps 4–5)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (p v : ι → Euclid P) (I : ι → Set ℝ) (c : ι → ℤ), (∀ k, ‖v k‖ = 1) → (∀ k, MeasurableSet (I k)) → ∀ R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, R.carrier = (⋃ k, ⋃ (_ : c k ≠ 0), (fun t : ℝ => p k + t • v k) '' I k) → (∀ x, R.mult x = ∑ k, ((fun t : ℝ => p k + t • v k) '' I k).indicator (fun _ => (c k).natAbs) x) → (∀ (x : Euclid P) (α : Covector (Euclid P) 1), (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x α = ∑ k, ((fun t : ℝ => p k + t • v k) '' I k).indicator (fun _ => (c k : ℝ)) x * α (fun _ => v k)) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, R.action (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) = ∑ k, (c k : ℝ) * ∫ t in I k, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (p k + t • v k) (fun _ => v k)) ∧ ∀ A : Set (Euclid P), MeasurableSet A → R.measure A = ∑ k, ENNReal.ofReal |(c k : ℝ)| * volume (I k ∩ (fun t : ℝ => p k + t • v k) ⁻¹' A)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent steps 4 (“R represents X”) and 5 (“Mass measure”), stated for any IMRep with the explicit carrier, multiplicity and θ·ξ identity. Uses the ancestor dependency idtp_fons_odc_line_hausdorff (the parent's dependency line_param).
Notation: γ_k(t) := p_k + t·v_k, S_k := γ_k(I_k), C := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, H¹ := μHE[1], ℒ¹ := volume on ℝ, and ev_v(α) := α(fun _ => v).
0. (Tools.) By idtp_fons_odc_line_hausdorff (second conjunct, for p_k, v_k with ‖v_k‖ = 1), γ_k is a measurable embedding, and for every J ⊆ ℝ, H¹⌞γ_k(J) = (γ_k)_#(ℒ¹⌞J) and H¹(γ_k(J)) = ℒ¹(J). Also γ_k is an isometry, since dist(γ_k s, γ_k t) = |s − t|·‖v_k‖ = |s − t|; hence it is continuous and a closed embedding.
1. S_k is measurable, as the image of the measurable set I_k under the measurable embedding γ_k. By the hypothesis C = ⋃_k ⋃_{c_k≠0} S_k, we have S_k ⊆ C whenever c_k ≠ 0.
2. (Integrability.) Fix ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P) and set g_k(x) := ω(x)(fun _ => v_k) = ev_{v_k}(ω(x)). Since ω is smooth with compact support and ev_{v_k} is continuous linear with ev_{v_k}(0) = 0, g_k is continuous with compact support. g_k is H¹-integrable on S_k: by the Tool, H¹⌞S_k = (γ_k)_#(ℒ¹⌞I_k). Since γ_k is a measurable embedding, integrability for this push-forward is equivalent to integrability of g_k∘γ_k for ℒ¹⌞I_k (MeasurableEmbedding.integrable_map_iff). And g_k∘γ_k is continuous with compact support because γ_k is a closed embedding, hence integrable on ℝ and on I_k.
3. (Action.) By definition, R.action(ω) = ∫_C θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH¹(x). By the θ·ξ hypothesis with α = ω(x), the integrand equals Σ_k 1_{S_k}(x)·c_k·g_k(x). Each summand can be written 1_{S_k}(x)·(c_k·g_k(x)), the indicator of the function c_k g_k. Each summand is integrable for H¹⌞C: by integrable_indicator_iff and Measure.restrict_restrict this reduces to integrability of c_k g_k on S_k ∩ C ⊆ S_k, which follows from step 2. Interchanging the finite sum with the integral (integral_finsetSum) gives R.action(ω) = Σ_k ∫_C 1_{S_k}(c_k g_k) dH¹ = Σ_k c_k·∫_{S_k ∩ C} g_k dH¹ (integral_indicator, Measure.restrict_restrict, integral_const_mul).
 - If c_k = 0, the k-th term is 0 = c_k·∫_{I_k} g_k(γ_k t) dt.
 - If c_k ≠ 0, then S_k ∩ C = S_k by step 1, and ∫_{S_k} g_k dH¹ = ∫ g_k d((γ_k)_#(ℒ¹⌞I_k)) = ∫_{I_k} g_k(γ_k t) dt (Tool and MeasurableEmbedding.integral_map).
 Hence R.action(ω) = Σ_k c_k ∫_{I_k} ω(p_k + t·v_k)(fun _ => v_k) dt, which is (i).
4. (Mass measure.) Let A be measurable. By definition R.measure = (H¹⌞C).withDensity θ, so R.measure(A) = ∫⁻_A θ d(H¹⌞C) = ∫⁻_{A ∩ C} θ dH¹ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). By the multiplicity hypothesis, as ℝ≥0∞-valued functions θ(x) = Σ_k 1_{S_k}(x)·|c_k|: cast the natural-number sum termwise (Nat.cast_sum), and the indicator commutes with the cast by a case split on x ∈ S_k. Then ∫⁻_{A∩C} θ dH¹ = Σ_k |c_k|·H¹(S_k ∩ (A ∩ C)) (lintegral_finsetSum, lintegral_indicator_const, Measure.restrict_apply). For each k, (|c_k| : ℝ≥0∞) = ENNReal.ofReal |(c_k : ℝ)| (Int.cast_abs, Nat.cast_natAbs, ENNReal.ofReal_natCast).
 - If c_k = 0, both k-th terms are 0.
 - If c_k ≠ 0, then S_k ⊆ C gives S_k ∩ (A ∩ C) = S_k ∩ A = γ_k(I_k ∩ γ_k⁻¹A) (image_inter_preimage). Its H¹-measure is ℒ¹(I_k ∩ γ_k⁻¹A) by the Tool with J = I_k ∩ γ_k⁻¹A.
 Summing, R.measure(A) = Σ_k ENNReal.ofReal |(c_k : ℝ)|·ℒ¹(I_k ∩ γ_k⁻¹(A)), which is (ii). ∎

R.action ω = ∫_C Σ 1_{S_k} c_k ω(x)(v_k) dH¹ = Σ c_k ∫_{S_k} ω(x)(v_k) dH¹ = Σ c_k ∫_{I_k} ω(γ_k t)(v_k) dt.
R.measure A = ∫⁻_{A∩C} θ dH¹ = Σ |c_k| H¹(S_k ∩ A ∩ C) = Σ |c_k| ℒ¹(I_k ∩ γ_k⁻¹A), where the c_k = 0 terms vanish on both sides.

subproblem.title: Weighted integrals of 1-forms along unit-speed lines define a 1-current (parent step 1)
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and ι a finite type. For each k ∈ ι let p_k, v_k ∈ ℝ^P with ‖v_k‖ = 1, let I_k ⊆ ℝ be an arbitrary set, and let c_k ∈ ℝ. Then there is a current X ∈ 𝒟_1(ℝ^P), that is, a GeometricCurrentOn univ 1: a linear functional on test 1-forms that is sequentially continuous at 0 for TestFormOnConverges. It satisfies X(ω) = Σ_k c_k·∫_{I_k} ω(p_k + t·v_k)(v_k) dt for every ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P). Here ω(y)(v) means ω(y)(fun _ => v), and ∫_{I_k} is the Bochner integral for Lebesgue measure restricted to I_k.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ι : Type) [Fintype ι] (p v : ι → Euclid P) (I : ι → Set ℝ) (c : ι → ℝ), (∀ k, ‖v k‖ = 1) → ∃ X : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) 1, X ω = ∑ k, c k * ∫ t in I k, (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) 1) (p k + t • v k) (fun _ => v k)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent step 1 (“Each piece is a current”), generalized to real coefficients and arbitrary parameter sets I_k; openness is not needed.
Notation: γ_k(t) := p_k + t·v_k. For a 1-covector α and v ∈ ℝ^P write α[v] := α(fun _ => v). Then ev_v : α ↦ α[v] is a continuous linear functional on Covector (Euclid P) 1 with ev_v(0) = 0 and |α[v]| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_{i : Fin 1} ‖v‖ = ‖α‖·‖v‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm).
1. (γ_k is an isometry.) dist(γ_k s, γ_k t) = ‖(s − t)·v_k‖ = |s − t|·‖v_k‖ = |s − t|. Hence γ_k is continuous and a closed embedding (Isometry.isClosedEmbedding), so γ_k⁻¹(K) is compact for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P (IsClosedEmbedding.isCompact_preimage).
2. (Integrability.) Fix k and ω ∈ 𝒟¹(ℝ^P); ω is C^∞, hence continuous, with compact support. The function g(t) := ω(γ_k t)[v_k] = ev_{v_k}(ω(γ_k t)) is continuous. By step 1, ω∘γ_k has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_isClosedEmbedding), and since ev_{v_k}(0) = 0 so does g (HasCompactSupport.comp_left). A continuous compactly supported function is Lebesgue integrable (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport), so g is integrable for volume restricted to I_k.
3. (Linearity.) Put X_k(ω) := ∫_{I_k} ω(γ_k t)[v_k] dt. For test forms ω, η and a ∈ ℝ we have (ω + η)(y)[v] = ω(y)[v] + η(y)[v] and (a·ω)(y)[v] = a·ω(y)[v]. All integrands are integrable by step 2, so integral_add and integral_const_mul give X_k(ω + η) = X_k(ω) + X_k(η) and X_k(a·ω) = a·X_k(ω). Thus X_k is a linear map TestFormOn univ 1 → ℝ.
4. (Null sequences converge uniformly on ℝ^P.) Suppose TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0. Then there is a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for all j, and for every order m, iteratedFDeriv ℝ m ω_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ m 0 = 0 uniformly on K. For m = 0, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f y is f y composed with a linear isometric equivalence (iteratedFDeriv_zero_eq_comp). So ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω_j y‖ = ‖ω_j(y)‖, and ω_j → 0 uniformly on K. For y ∉ K, y ∉ tsupport ω_j, so ω_j(y) = 0 for all j (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). Therefore ω_j → 0 uniformly on all of ℝ^P: for every ε > 0, eventually ‖ω_j(y)‖ < ε for all y.
5. (Sequential continuity of X_k.) Let ω_j → 0 as in step 4 and put F_j(t) := ω_j(γ_k t)[v_k]. Apply dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_filter_of_dominated_convergence) for the measure volume.restrict I_k, with limit function 0 and bound b := 1_{γ_k⁻¹(K)} (indicator of the constant 1). The hypotheses hold:
 (a) each F_j is a.e. strongly measurable, being continuous by step 2;
 (b) by step 4 with ε = 1, eventually ‖ω_j(y)‖ < 1 for all y. For such j and all t: if γ_k t ∈ K then |F_j(t)| ≤ ‖ω_j(γ_k t)‖·‖v_k‖ ≤ 1 = b(t); if γ_k t ∉ K then γ_k t ∉ tsupport ω_j, so F_j(t) = 0 ≤ b(t);
 (c) b is integrable: γ_k⁻¹(K) is compact by step 1, hence closed (measurable) with finite Lebesgue measure. So the indicator of 1 on it is integrable (integrableOn_const, integrable_indicator), and so is its restriction to I_k;
 (d) for every t, F_j(t) → 0, because ω_j(γ_k t) → 0 (step 4, TendstoUniformly.tendsto_at) and ev_{v_k} is continuous with ev_{v_k}(0) = 0.
 Hence X_k(ω_j) = ∫_{I_k} F_j → ∫_{I_k} 0 = 0. This is exactly the field continuous' of GeometricCurrentOn univ 1. So X_k, the linear map of step 3 with this continuity, is a GeometricCurrentOn univ 1 with X_k(ω) = ∫_{I_k} ω(p_k + t·v_k)[v_k] dt.
6. (Weighted finite sum.) Choose such an X_k for each k (choice over the finite type ι). Let X have underlying linear map Σ_k c_k·(X_k as a linear map). If TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0, then each X_k(ω_j) → 0 by step 5, so c_k·X_k(ω_j) → 0 (Tendsto.const_mul) and Σ_k c_k·X_k(ω_j) → 0 (tendsto_finsetSum). So X is a GeometricCurrentOn univ 1, and for every ω, X(ω) = Σ_k c_k·X_k(ω) = Σ_k c_k·∫_{I_k} ω(p_k + t·v_k)[v_k] dt. ∎
Formalization note: GeometricCurrentOn is the structure ⟨toCurrent, continuous'⟩. Here toCurrent is a LinearMap (toFun, map_add', map_smul'), and continuous' requires Tendsto (fun j => toCurrent (ωs j)) atTop (𝓝 0) whenever TestFormOnConverges ωs 0.
proof_key_steps: γ_k(t) = p_k + t v_k is an isometry, hence a closed embedding with compact preimages of compact sets.
For a test form ω, t ↦ ω(γ_k t)(v_k) is continuous with compact support, hence integrable on I_k, and X_k(ω) := ∫_{I_k} ω(γ_k t)(v_k) dt is linear.
TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 gives a common compact K and uniform convergence of the 0-th iterated derivative on K, hence ω_j → 0 uniformly on ℝ^P.
Dominated convergence with bound 1_{γ_k⁻¹K} gives X_k(ω_j) → 0, so X_k is a GeometricCurrentOn univ 1.
X := Σ_k c_k X_k is continuous by tendsto_finsetSum and satisfies the stated formula.

subproblem.title: A set agreeing near x with the affine plane x + Q has Q as approximate tangent space at x (parent step 3e)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let M ⊆ ℝ^P be measurable, x ∈ ℝ^P, Q ⊆ ℝ^P a linear subspace with finrank Q = n, and r > 0. Suppose M ∩ B_r(x) = {y : y − x ∈ Q} ∩ B_r(x), where B_r(x) is the open ball. Then HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q holds (Simon Ch. 3, Def. 1.4): finrank Q = n and, for every f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P), ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M)} f dHⁿ → ∫_Q f dHⁿ as ρ ↓ 0. Here η_{x,ρ}(y) = ρ⁻¹(y − x) is blowUpMap x ρ and Hⁿ = μHE[n].

Here it is stated for a general n-dimensional subspace Q (Simon Ch. 3, Definition 1.4).
1. The dimension condition finrank ℝ Q = n is a hypothesis. It remains to prove the limit for an arbitrary f ∈ C_c(ℝ^P).
2. The topological support of f is compact, hence bounded. So there is R₀ > 0 with tsupport f ⊆ closedBall(0, R₀) (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_closedBall_lt applied to the compact support).
3. For ρ > 0, η_{x,ρ}(M) = {y : x + ρ·y ∈ M}. If z ∈ M, then y := ρ⁻¹(z − x) satisfies x + ρ·y = z ∈ M. Conversely, if x + ρ·y ∈ M then η_{x,ρ}(x + ρ·y) = ρ⁻¹(ρ·y) = y.
4. Let 0 < ρ < r/R₀, so that ρ·R₀ < r. For y ∈ tsupport f, ‖(x + ρ·y) − x‖ = ρ‖y‖ ≤ ρR₀ < r, so x + ρ·y ∈ B_r(x). By the hypothesis M ∩ B_r(x) = {z : z − x ∈ Q} ∩ B_r(x), we get x + ρ·y ∈ M ⟺ (x + ρ·y) − x = ρ·y ∈ Q ⟺ y ∈ Q. The last equivalence holds because Q is a subspace and ρ ≠ 0: if ρ·y ∈ Q then y = ρ⁻¹·(ρ·y) ∈ Q, and if y ∈ Q then ρ·y ∈ Q.
5. The set {y : x + ρ·y ∈ M} is measurable, as the preimage of the measurable set M under the continuous map y ↦ x + ρ·y. Q is closed (Submodule.closed_of_finiteDimensional), hence measurable. By integral_indicator, ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫ 1_{η_{x,ρ}(M)}·f dHⁿ and ∫_Q f dHⁿ = ∫ 1_Q·f dHⁿ. The two integrands agree at every y: on tsupport f the indicators take the same value by step 4, and off tsupport f both integrands vanish since f(y) = 0. Hence ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M)} f dHⁿ = ∫_Q f dHⁿ for every ρ ∈ (0, r/R₀).
6. The interval (0, r/R₀) belongs to the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (Ioo_mem_nhdsGT, since r/R₀ > 0). So the function ρ ↦ ∫_{η_{x,ρ}(M)} f dHⁿ is eventually equal to the constant ∫_Q f dHⁿ, and therefore tends to it as ρ ↓ 0 (tendsto_const_nhds.congr'). Since f was arbitrary, this together with step 1 is HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q. ∎

For ρ > 0, η_{x,ρ}(M) = {y : x + ρy ∈ M}.
For 0 < ρ < r/R₀ and y ∈ spt f, x + ρy ∈ B_r(x), so x + ρy ∈ M ⟺ ρy ∈ Q ⟺ y ∈ Q.
Hence the blown-up integral equals ∫_Q f dHⁿ for all small ρ, and the limit in Definition 1.4 holds trivially.

1. Since x ∈ S_k, x = p_k + t₀·v_k for some t₀ ∈ I_k. As I_k is open, there is ε > 0 with B_ε(t₀) = (t₀ − ε, t₀ + ε) ⊆ I_k (Metric.isOpen_iff).
2. For each j ≠ k we have x ∉ closure(S_j). By mem_closure_iff_frequently, this says it is not frequently true near x that y ∈ S_j; that is, eventually in 𝓝 x, y ∉ S_j. By Metric.eventually_nhds_iff there is δ > 0 such that every y with dist(y, x) < δ lies in no S_j with j ≠ k.
3. Put r := min(ε, δ) > 0. (⊆) Let y ∈ M with dist(y, x) < r. Since M ⊆ ⋃_j S_j, y ∈ S_j for some j. Since dist(y, x) < r ≤ δ, step 2 forces j = k. So y = p_k + t·v_k with t ∈ I_k, and y − x = t·v_k − t₀·v_k = (t − t₀)·v_k ∈ span{v_k}.
4. (⊇) Let y ∈ B_r(x) with y − x ∈ span{v_k}. By Submodule.mem_span_singleton, y − x = s·v_k for some s ∈ ℝ. Then y = p_k + (t₀ + s)·v_k. Using ‖v_k‖ = 1, |s| = |s|·‖v_k‖ = ‖s·v_k‖ = dist(y, x) < r ≤ ε. So |(t₀ + s) − t₀| < ε, i.e. t₀ + s ∈ B_ε(t₀) ⊆ I_k. Hence y ∈ S_k ⊆ M, so y ∈ M ∩ B_r(x).
5. Steps 3 and 4 give M ∩ B_r(x) = {y : y − x ∈ span{v_k}} ∩ B_r(x) with r > 0. ∎

Finitely many j ≠ k with x ∉ closure S_j give δ > 0 such that B_δ(x) misses every S_j with j ≠ k.
With r = min(ε, δ), every point of M ∩ B_r(x) lies on S_k, hence on x + span{v_k}.
Conversely, x + s v_k with |s| < r equals γ_k(t₀ + s) ∈ S_k ⊆ M.
